text:
Pierre-Luc Dubois has goals in three straight games, including a top-shelf finish against New Jersey on Thursday and the game-tying goal against Ottawa on Tuesday. After a 2025-26 in which he played only 29 games for Washington, 11 points in 12 games this season is a welcome sight for the Capitals.

How much of it will last is a fair question. He is scoring on 20% of his shots, above our range for him, and Washington has scored 5.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. His 3.3 points per 60 sits above the top of what we would expect (about 3.1). Twenty shots in 12 games is not a big volume for a top-six forward.

The good news is underneath. The Capitals are taking 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him out there, 6.6 points better than without him, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 71% of his entries in a small sample. Evolving-Hockey noted he drew top competition (98th percentile) last season. The shooting is likely to cool; whether that chance share holds is the real test.
